title: The Stolen Blessing
reflectionText: The voice was Jacob's voice, but the hands were the hands of Esau — and the blessing, once spoken, could not be called back. Then came the cry, great and bitter: Bless me — me also, my father. What is it to stand where Esau stood, asking whether there is only one blessing?
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch A (journey backlog G9, approved 2026-07-22). Genesis 27, absent both lanes (verified 0 anchor hits); right-adjacent neighbor 1018 (Genesis 28:10-22, Jacob's Ladder) picks up after the flight. Boundary: chapter 27 only — no birthright backstory from Genesis 25, no Bethel material from Genesis 28, and the 25:23 oracle is NOT imported as Rebekah's motive; her motive is left unstated as in the source. SHORT + FULL + LONG (WEB 457w / 863w / 1100w; KJV 498w / 899w / 932w): the 46-verse dialogue-dense chapter (~1161 WEB source words) honestly supports all three bands. LONG renders the charge, the scheme, the three verification probes, both blessings, and both Rebekah speeches; FULL compresses Isaac's reply (v37) and the anti-blessing (vv39-40) to reported speech; SHORT compresses the scheme and omits v46 (the daughters-of-Heth complaint) — documented compression. All emotion is source-stated (Isaac trembled violently; Esau's exceedingly great and bitter cry and weeping; Esau's hatred; Rebekah weary of her life). No invented interiority for Jacob. CODEX-AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-07-23 (Finding 1, accepted as genuine ADR-031 L2 failure). First remediation (commit 987e9c36) reduced literal reconstruction (run 33/84.8% -> 10/40.8%) but the re-audit judged the macro structure still verse-mapped and flagged newly-introduced unsupported detail. SECOND REMEDIATION (this commit): the KJV LONG was re-authored again from a private scene outline into six scene-based movements — the whole scheme (vv1-17) folded into one summary movement, then the bedside deception (vv18-25), the blessing (vv26-29), the discovery and Isaac's trembling (vv30-33), Esau's grief and plea (vv34-38), and the lesser blessing with the flight (vv39-46). Connective material is heavily compressed and paragraphs are organized by scene rather than verse boundary; canonical event chronology is preserved (events not reordered). Current metrics: run 16 (the blessing's own enumerated gifts, v28) / coverage 30.7% / 932w. Every unsupported addition the re-audit named was removed: no ascribed Rebekah motive beyond her stated instruction (vv9-10); no Isaac 'moved' / 'full heart' / 'drew close'; no invented tent. Essential turning-point dialogue kept direct (voice-vs-hands; 'Bless me, even me also, O my father'; 'Hast thou but one blessing'). WEB SHORT/FULL/LONG and KJV SHORT/FULL unchanged.
